question: Which responsibility and completion-phase declarations are necessary before comparing synchronous writeback and batch handoff?
phase_rules: Handoff may be rejected; phases are not a universal success-only linear pipeline.
Callback acceptance and helper return do not establish I/O end or completion accounting.
Completion accounting is not a durability barrier.
Dropping completion performs unsuccessful zero-prefix accounting, not waiting for I/O.
required_provider_fields: return-value guarantee phase, including empty/no-work cases
budget event and unit, including rejected submissions
completion obligation carrier, split and drop behavior
drain owner and required exit boundaries
error categories and deferred-error reporting owner
lifetime protection object and required duration

propositions.claim: submit_cache_pages can return with an outstanding batch
propositions.measurement: helper return, pending batch count, folio writeback state, later completion
budget before callback, callback rejection, budget after; need explicit assertion if existing tests omit it

propositions.claim: later rejected batch does not end prior retained I/O
propositions.measurement: first retained batch state, second rejection/redirty, later first-batch completion or drop after I/O end

propositions.claim: WritebackCompletion::complete is not a durability proof
propositions.measurement: declared non-guarantee; no device persistence or crash test in this batch

first_batch: Archive fixed primary sources and audit existing test assertions; do not invent another toy simulator before checking reuse feasibility.
planned_execution: Next preflight the original test harness and dependencies; distinguish original-test execution, extracted logic and modeled replacements. No production/config mutation implied.
limits: All declarations researcher-transcribed, no provider approval; source review is not executed evidence; shared downstream helper does not prove selected wrappers interchangeable; no ownership-design correctness or novelty claim.
stop: Complete all four proposition evidence mappings, retain unexecuted and missing assertions, no new performance score.
